en: to be slender; to be slim

examples.en: That actor is tall and slender.

examples.ko: 동생은 호리호리한 체격이라 옷이 잘 어울려요.
examples.en: My younger brother is slim, so clothes look good on him.
He looks slim, but he's strong.
I exercise every day to keep a slender figure.
He is a slender young man with a fair face.

examples.ko: 어릴 때는 호리호리했는데 지금은 많이 쪘어요.
examples.en: I was slim as a kid, but I've put on a lot of weight now.

explain: 키가 크면서 몸이 가늘고 날렵한 모습에 어울려요. '날씬하다'가 살이 적고 보기 좋다는 느낌이라면, '호리호리하다'는 길쭉하고 가는 몸매를 그려요. '마르다'는 때때로 걱정스러운 느낌이 있어서 말투가 달라요.

phrases.en: I envy that model's slender body.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서는 '호리호리한'으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Before a noun, use 'horihorihan'.

phrases.example: 검은 옷을 입으면 더 호리호리해 보여요.
phrases.en: You look slimmer when you wear black clothes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습이 그렇게 보인다고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone appears slender.

phrases.en: I work out, so I'm not slender anymore.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 몸이 가늘지 않다고 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form says the body is not slim.

explain_en: It suits a body that is tall, thin, and lithe. '날씬하다' feels like being slim in a nice way, while '호리호리하다' paints a long, slender build. '마르다' can sound worrisome, so the tone is different.

t90.ax: That actor is tall and slender.

en: to persist in; to hold fast to

examples.en: The child insists on only his own opinion to the end.
He kept sticking to the old way.
If you stick to just one thing, your options get narrow.
The shop is particular about taste, so the ingredients are good.
There is no reason to insist on only that method.
Perhaps sticking to it paid off, because the result was good.

explain: '고집'은 명사로도 써서 '고집이 세다'라고 해요. 고집하다는 남의 말을 듣지 않고 자기 생각을 지킬 때라 보통 부정적이지만, 맛·품질처럼 신념을 지킬 때는 긍정적으로도 써요. 앞에는 '을/를'이 와요.

phrases.en: My younger sibling keeps being stubborn.
phrases.nuance_ko: '고집하다'와 비슷하게 자기 뜻을 굽히지 않을 때 쓰는 명사 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun phrase with a similar meaning: not giving up your own way.

phrases.en: Please don't hold on only to your own opinion.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대에게 부드럽게 부탁하거나 조언하는 부정 명령이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite negative command used to advise someone.

phrases.en: That shop sticks to the old taste.
phrases.nuance_ko: 신념을 지키는 긍정적인 느낌으로도 쓸 수 있는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing that can have a positive feel of keeping to a principle.
phrases.en_equiv: to stick to the old taste

explain_en: '고집' is also a noun, as in '고집이 세다' (stubborn). 'Gojiphada' is keeping your own idea without listening to others, which is usually negative but can be positive for beliefs such as taste or quality. It takes the object marker 을/를.

examples.en: He keeps denying the facts.
The company denied the rumor.
You must not deny your own mistake.
No one could deny those words.
I only heard answers that denied it.
You cannot deny this result.

explain: 사실이나 존재를 아니라고 말할 때 써요. '사실을 부정하다'처럼 목적어와 함께 써요. 반대말은 '인정하다'예요. 소리가 같은 '부정(不正)'은 옳지 않은 일이라는 다른 말이에요.

phrases.en: He didn't deny his mistake.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아니라고 하지 않고 받아들였다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means he didn't say no and accepted it.

phrases.en: He strongly denies the rumor.
phrases.nuance_ko: 분명하고 힘 있게 아니라고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when saying no clearly and firmly.

phrases.example: 그는 그 이야기가 사실이 아니라고 말했어요.
phrases.en: He said the story is not true.
phrases.nuance_ko: '부정하다'를 쉬운 말로 풀어서 일상 대화에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A plain-language way to say '부정하다' in everyday talk.

explain_en: It is used when you say something is not true or does not exist, with an object as in '사실을 부정하다'. The opposite is '인정하다'. The same-sounding '부정(不正)' is a different word meaning wrongdoing.

gh: deny an accusation or a fact

p.n: 부인하다 is possible here but sounds more like denying a claim than rejecting existence.

examples.en: I was persuaded by my friend's sincere words.
I'm the kind of person who gets persuaded easily.

examples.ko: 설명을 듣고 나니 설득될 수밖에 없었어요.
examples.en: After hearing the explanation, I couldn't help but be convinced.
No matter what I said, he wasn't persuaded.
My parents, once persuaded, finally gave permission.
If you show the data, the other person gets convinced.

explain: '설득하다'는 설득하는 사람, '설득되다'는 마음이 바뀐 사람의 입장이에요. 말할 때는 '넘어가다', '마음이 바뀌다'도 많이 써요. '이해되다'는 뜻을 알겠다는 것이라 달라요.

phrases.en: I persuaded my friend and we went together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음을 바꾸게 하는 사람 쪽에서 쓰는 말이에요. '설득되다'와 짝이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the side of the person who changes someone's mind. It pairs with 설득되다.

phrases.en: After hearing that, I changed my mind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때 '설득되다' 대신 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in speech instead of 설득되다.

phrases.en: I'm not convinced by that reason.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대의 말에 마음이 움직이지 않을 때 쓰는 부정형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, used when someone's words don't move you.

explain_en: '설득하다' is the persuader's side; '설득되다' is the side whose mind was changed. In speech, '넘어가다' or '마음이 바뀌다' are also common. '이해되다' is different: it only means 'it makes sense'.

examples.en: Nobody knows the real story behind that person.

examples.ko: 회사 속사정을 알고 나니 이해가 됐어요.
examples.en: After learning the company's inside situation, I understood.
He smiles on the outside, but his real situation is complicated.
I asked whether there was some hidden circumstance.

examples.ko: 남의 집 속사정을 함부로 말하지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't carelessly talk about another family's private affairs.
You don't even know the real story, yet you get angry first.

explain: '사정'은 일의 형편 전체이고, 속사정은 겉으로 드러나지 않은 숨은 사정이에요. '속내'는 마음속 생각에 가깝고, 속사정은 처한 형편이나 이유에 가까워요.

phrases.example: 다들 말은 안 해도 속사정이 있을 거예요.
phrases.en: Everyone probably has their own situation even if they don't say it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉으로 보이지 않는 이유가 있다고 짐작할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you guess there is a hidden reason behind something.

phrases.en: I told my friend about my family's private situation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 숨기던 형편을 이야기할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you share a situation you had kept hidden.

phrases.en: Don't talk when you don't know the real situation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사정을 모르는 사람에게 조언하거나 말릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to caution someone who doesn't know the real circumstances.

explain_en: '사정' is a circumstance in general, while 속사정 is the hidden circumstance not visible from outside. '속내' is closer to inner thoughts and feelings, whereas 속사정 is closer to the situation or reason behind something.

t90.ax: Nobody knows the real story behind that person.

examples.ko: 책을 읽다가 마음에 와닿는 문장을 적어 두었어요.
examples.en: While reading, I wrote down a sentence that struck a chord with me.

examples.ko: 비 오는 밤에는 노래 가사가 더 가슴에 와닿아요.
examples.en: On rainy nights, song lyrics hit home even more.
Only now did the teacher's advice really sink in.
If I only hear it in numbers, it doesn't really register.

examples.ko: 그 영화의 마지막 대사가 유난히 마음에 와닿았어요.
examples.en: The last line of that movie especially touched me.

examples.ko: 직접 겪어 보니 그 말이 확 와닿네요.
examples.en: Now that I've experienced it myself, those words really hit me.

explain: 어떤 말이나 이야기가 머리로만이 아니라 마음으로 느껴질 때 써요. '와 닿다'로 띄어 쓰지 않고 붙여서 써요. 부정형 '와닿지 않아요'는 '실감이 안 나요'와 비슷하게 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: That story doesn't really resonate with me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음으로 실감이 안 날 때 쓰는 부정형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, for when something doesn't feel real to you.

phrases.en: Today the teacher's words touched my heart.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 마음으로 느꼈다는 과거형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The past form, saying that you already felt it in your heart.

phrases.en: I like stories that touch me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 명사를 붙여 '마음에 느껴지는 ~'라는 뜻을 만들어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Attached to a noun to mean something that touches the heart.

explain_en: It is used when words or stories are felt in the heart, not just understood in the head. It is written as one word, not '와 닿다'. The negative '와닿지 않아요' is often used much like '실감이 안 나요' (it doesn't feel real).

en: to be doubtful; to be questionable; to be suspicious

examples.en: What that person says seems a bit questionable.

examples.ko: 의심쩍은 문자는 열어 보지 말고 지우세요.
examples.en: Don't open suspicious text messages, just delete them.
The price was so cheap that it actually felt suspicious.

examples.ko: 점원이 의심쩍다는 듯이 영수증을 다시 봤어요.
examples.en: The clerk looked at the receipt again as if doubtful.
If you have doubts, check for yourself.

examples.ko: 이야기가 앞뒤가 안 맞아서 의심쩍게 들렸어요.
examples.en: The story didn't add up, so it sounded doubtful.

explain: '의심스럽다'와 뜻이 가깝고 '미심쩍다'도 비슷해요. 믿기 어렵거나 이상해서 마음이 개운하지 않을 때 써요. '의심쩍은 눈으로 보다', '의심쩍은 점이 있다'처럼 써요.

phrases.example: 가게 주인이 저를 의심쩍은 눈으로 봤어요.
phrases.en: The shop owner looked at me with suspicious eyes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 믿지 못하는 마음이 눈빛에 드러날 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when distrust shows in someone's gaze.

phrases.example: 그 사람의 설명은 하나도 의심쩍지 않았어요.
phrases.en: His explanation wasn't doubtful at all.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 써서 믿을 만하다는 뜻을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form shows that something seems trustworthy.

phrases.en: This price is so cheap that it seems suspicious.
phrases.nuance_ko: '의심쩍다'와 뜻이 가깝고 더 널리 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Close in meaning to 의심쩍다 and more widely used.

explain_en: It is close in meaning to '의심스럽다', and '미심쩍다' is similar. Use it when something is hard to believe or seems off and leaves you uneasy. Typical uses are '의심쩍은 눈으로 보다' and '의심쩍은 점이 있다'.

examples.en: I received career counseling at school.

examples.ko: 스트레스가 심해서 카운슬링을 받아 보기로 했어요.
examples.en: I was so stressed that I decided to try counseling.
Thanks to the counseling, I feel much more at ease.

examples.ko: 우리 회사는 직원 카운슬링 시간을 운영해요.
examples.en: Our company runs counseling hours for employees.

examples.ko: 카운슬링을 하는 선생님이 친절하게 들어 주셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher who does counseling listened to me kindly.

examples.ko: 이 센터에서 무료 카운슬링을 해 줘요.
examples.en: This center offers free counseling.

explain: '상담'으로 바꿔 말해도 돼요. 카운슬링은 마음 고민이나 진로처럼 이야기를 들어 주고 조언하는 상담에 잘 어울려요. '카운슬링을 받다/하다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: I had career counseling with my teacher.
phrases.nuance_ko: '카운슬링'과 바꿔 쓸 수 있는 한자어이고, 더 널리 쓰여요.
phrases.nuance_en: A Sino-Korean word interchangeable with 카운슬링, and more widely used.

phrases.en: I've been feeling down lately, so I'm getting counseling.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상담을 듣는 사람 입장에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the point of view of the person receiving counseling.

phrases.en: I want to sign up for career counseling.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학교나 회사에서 진로 고민을 상담할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Commonly used at schools or workplaces for career-related concerns.

explain_en: You can often replace it with '상담'. '카운슬링' suits sessions where someone listens and advises on worries or career choices. It goes with '카운슬링을 받다/하다'.

examples.en: Planes take off following instructions from the control tower.
The control tower and the pilot are communicating by radio.

examples.ko: 공항 관제탑이 한눈에 보이는 카페에 갔어요.
examples.en: I went to a cafe with a clear view of the airport control tower.
To work in a control tower, you have to pass an exam.

examples.ko: 관제탑은 활주로가 잘 보이는 높은 곳에 있어요.
examples.en: The control tower is in a high place with a good view of the runways.
I have an uncle who works in a control tower.

explain: 공항에서 비행기의 이착륙을 알려 주는 곳이에요. 뉴스에서는 조직의 중심 역할을 비유할 때 '컨트롤타워'라는 외래어도 많이 써요.

phrases.en: The airport control tower sends signals to the planes.
phrases.nuance_ko: '관제탑'이 어디에 있는지 분명히 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to make clear where the control tower is.

phrases.en: A control tower staff member checked the weather.
phrases.nuance_ko: 관제탑에서 일하는 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a person who works in the control tower.

phrases.en: That agency is the control tower for responding to the accident.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 조직의 중심 역할을 비유할 때 쓰는 외래어예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A loanword used in news to figuratively mean a central command role.

explain_en: It is the place at an airport that directs planes taking off and landing. In the news, the loanword '컨트롤타워' is also used as a metaphor for the central body of an organization.

en: of course; well, as for that

examples.en: Well, of course we should help.
Well, the teacher knows best, of course.

examples.ko: 그야 저도 가고 싶지만 시간이 없어요.
examples.en: Sure, I want to go too, but I don't have time.
Is it tasty? Well, you'll know when you try it.
Well, of course it's nice to have a lot of money.
Why was I late? Well, because the road was jammed.

explain: 대답이나 설명 앞에 붙여서 '그건 말할 필요도 없죠'라는 느낌을 줘요. '그야 당연하죠', '그야 그렇죠'처럼 굳어진 표현으로 많이 써요. '그야말로'(정말로)는 이 말과 다른 단어예요.

phrases.en: "Do you want to go together?" "Of course."
phrases.nuance_ko: '그야' 뒤에 붙는 가장 흔한 말로, 말할 필요도 없다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase with 그야, meaning it goes without saying.

phrases.en: Well, sure, that's true. I know that too.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대 말에 동의하지만 조금 덧붙일 말이 있을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to agree with someone while hinting that there is more to say.

phrases.en: Can you help me? Of course.
phrases.nuance_ko: '그야'보다 단순하게 '당연해요'라고 대답하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simpler way to say 'of course', without the 'as for that' feeling of 그야.

explain_en: Placed before an answer or explanation, it gives the feeling of 'that goes without saying'. It appears often in set phrases like '그야 당연하죠' and '그야 그렇죠'. '그야말로' (truly) is a different word, so don't mix them up.

p.n: 물론 is neutral and works in any register; 그야 adds a 'that goes without saying' tone.

t90.ax: Well, of course we should help.

examples.en: Since the fight, we act like strangers.
He was a stranger I met on the street, but I helped him.

examples.ko: 가족이어도 말을 안 하면 남남 같아요.
examples.en: Even family feels like strangers if you don't talk.
We share a family name, but we aren't related.

examples.ko: 한 집에 살아도 남남처럼 지내는 부부가 있어요.
examples.en: Some couples live in one house but act like strangers.

examples.ko: 남남끼리 만나서 가족이 되는 게 결혼이에요.
examples.en: Marriage is when two people who were strangers become a family.

explain: '타인'보다 부드러운 입말이고 '남이다'와 비슷하게 써요. 서로 가까운 사이였다가 멀어졌을 때도 '남남이 되다'로 말해요.

phrases.en: If we break up, we become strangers again.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가깝던 사이가 완전히 끊어져서 아무 관계도 없게 된다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means a once-close relationship is completely cut off.

explain_en: It is a softer spoken word than '타인' and is used like '남이다'. It is also used when people who were once close drift apart, as in '남남이 되다'.

examples.ko: 올림픽에서 한국 양궁은 단체전 금메달을 땄어요.
examples.en: At the Olympics, Korean archery won gold in the team event.
The team event is more nerve-racking than the individual event.
Our team came third in the team event.

examples.ko: 내일 단체전이 있어서 일찍 자야 해요.
examples.en: I have a team event tomorrow, so I have to sleep early.
Table tennis is divided into individual and team events.

examples.ko: 단체전은 한 명이 못해도 동료가 도와줄 수 있어요.
examples.en: In a team event, teammates can help out even if one person does poorly.

explain: 반대말은 '개인전'이에요. 양궁, 탁구, 체조처럼 한 종목 안에 개인전과 단체전이 같이 있는 경기가 많아요. 단체전은 팀 점수를 합쳐서 순위를 정하고, 뉴스에서는 '단체전 금메달'처럼 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: The team event match is this evening.
phrases.nuance_ko: 팀으로 하는 경기를 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a match played as a team.

phrases.en: Our school is entering the table tennis team event.
phrases.nuance_ko: 참가할 때 '나가다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 'go out' for participating.

phrases.en: I'm more comfortable with the individual event than the team event.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite word.

explain_en: The opposite is 개인전. Many sports, such as archery, table tennis and gymnastics, have both an individual and a team event. In a 단체전 the team's scores are added up to decide the ranking, and the news often says '단체전 금메달'.

en: to be lukewarm; to be tepid

examples.en: The bath water was lukewarm, so I heated it more.
The coffee cooled down and is lukewarm.
I drank a glass of lukewarm barley tea.
Don't answer that question in a half-hearted way.
It tastes bad if it's lukewarm, so I'll microwave it.
It rained, and even the air felt lukewarm.

explain: 뜨겁지도 차갑지도 않아서 어중간한 온도에 써요. 비슷한 말 '미지근하다'도 있고, 둘 다 온도뿐 아니라 시원하지 않은 반응이나 태도에도 말해요.

phrases.en: Customers' reactions are lukewarm.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기대만큼 뜨겁지 않고 별로 관심이 없는 반응을 말할 때 써요. 온도와 상관없이 쓰는 비유예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a reaction that isn't as enthusiastic as hoped. It is a figurative use unrelated to temperature.

explain_en: It is used for a temperature that is neither hot nor cold. A similar word is '미지근하다', and both can describe not only temperature but also a half-hearted reaction or attitude.

t90.ax: The coffee cooled down and is lukewarm.
